group.title: Getting around
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A machine with wings that flies people through the air.
examples: Our {plane} lands at six o’clock.
wrong: We drove the plane under the sea.

words.meaning: A train that goes under the ground in a city.
examples: I take the {metro} to work every day.
wrong: The metro is a train that flies above the clouds.

words.meaning: A place where you can sit.
examples: Is this {seat} free?
wrong: I put the seat on my head and wore it.

words.meaning: A big, heavy bike with an engine.
examples: He rides a red {motorcycle} to work.
wrong: My motorcycle has no engine, so I push the pedals.

words.meaning: A round thing under a car or bike that turns.
examples: A bike has two {wheels}.
wrong: The wheel was square, so the car moved fast.

words.meaning: A time when you go to a place and come back.
examples: We took a {trip} to the beach.
wrong: The trip took us nowhere at all.

words.meaning: A small truck for carrying things or people.
examples: They moved the sofa in a {van}.
wrong: My van is as small as a pen.

words.meaning: The part of a car that makes it move.
examples: The car’s {engine} is very loud.
wrong: The car has no engine because it moves.

words.meaning: The black rubber ring around a car or bike wheel.
examples: My bike has a flat {tire}.
wrong: I filled the tire with milk.

words.meaning: The part of a car that makes a loud warning sound.
examples: The driver used the {horn} at the dog.
wrong: The horn makes the car go faster.

words.meaning: The space at the back of a car for bags.
examples: Put the bags in the {trunk}.
wrong: The driver sits in the trunk.

words.meaning: A small vehicle with two small wheels that you stand on.
examples: She rides her {scooter} to school.
wrong: I put my scooter in my pocket.

words.meaning: A place where trains stop for people to get on and off.
examples: The {train station} is near the river.
wrong: Planes land at the train station.

words.meaning: A place where many buses start and stop.
examples: I’ll meet you at the {bus station}.
wrong: Boats leave from the bus station.

words.meaning: A place where you buy tickets.
examples: Buy your tickets at the {ticket office}.
wrong: The ticket office sells fruit and flowers.

words.meaning: A long, hard way for cars to drive on.
examples: This {road} goes to the beach.
wrong: The car drove on the road under the water.

words.meaning: A sign at the side of a road that gives drivers information.
examples: The {road sign} says go slow.
wrong: I read a road sign in my kitchen.

words.meaning: To go into a car or taxi.
examples: {Get in}, I’ll drive you home.
wrong: I got in the car and stayed outside.

words.meaning: To leave a bus, train or bike.
examples: We {get off} at the next stop.
wrong: I got off the bus and stayed on it.

words.meaning: To leave a car or taxi.
examples: Let’s {get out} of the car here.
wrong: I got out of the car and sat inside it.

words.meaning: To leave a car in a place for a time.
examples: You can {park} your car here.
wrong: I parked the car by driving it all day.

words.meaning: Using a bus to travel.
examples: I go to school {by bus}.
wrong: I came by bus, so I walked all the way.

words.meaning: Using a car to travel.
examples: We went to the lake {by car}.
wrong: We went by car and flew there.

words.meaning: To travel somewhere on a bus.
examples: I {take the bus} to work.
wrong: I take the bus, so I walk the whole way.

words.meaning: The place where a bus or train stops after this one.
examples: The {next stop} is the city center.
wrong: The next stop was the stop we just left.

words.meaning: To change direction to the left side.
examples: {Turn left} at the bank.
wrong: Turn left, and then you go right.

words.meaning: To change direction to the right side.
examples: {Turn right} at the corner.
wrong: I turned right, so I went left.

words.meaning: To keep going the same way without turning.
examples: {Go straight} for two blocks.
wrong: Go straight, and turn at every corner.

words.meaning: Words that tell you how to get to a place.
examples: Can you give me {directions} to the station?
wrong: I followed the directions and the food tasted good.

words.meaning: The road or path you take to get somewhere.
examples: Is this the {way} to the station?
wrong: The way to the station is a kind of fruit.

words.meaning: When a car or bus hits something by mistake.
examples: Nobody was hurt in the car {accident}.
wrong: We planned the accident for a week.

words.meaning: A flying machine with long blades that turn on top.
examples: The {helicopter} landed on the roof.
wrong: The helicopter swam down the river.

words.meaning: A card that shows you can drive a car.
examples: You need a {driver’s license} to drive.
wrong: My baby brother has a driver’s license.

words.meaning: A small metal thing you use to open and start a car.
examples: I can’t find my {car key}.
wrong: I started the car with my car key in my bag at home.

words.meaning: A car you pay to take you somewhere.
examples: Let’s take a {cab} to the airport.
wrong: We took a cab, so we walked home.

words.meaning: At the right time, not late.
examples: The train left {on time}.
wrong: The bus came on time, an hour late.

words.meaning: Not fast.
examples: Drive {slowly} near the school.
wrong: The car drove slowly at top speed.

words.meaning: A small paper or card that lets you ride a bus.
examples: I showed my {bus ticket} to the driver.
wrong: I ate my bus ticket for lunch.

words.meaning: A road or path made only for bicycles.
examples: We rode along the {bike path} by the river.
wrong: Big trucks drive on the bike path.

words.meaning: The seat behind the driver in a car.
examples: The kids sit in the {back seat}.
wrong: The driver steers the car from the back seat.
